items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: At the same time the material was shown to Louie Lipstone who was running the Paramount music department and Louie wanted us there, so suddenly we had a contract with Paramount

ctx.x: I decided to take a crack at songwriting, she said she knew Johnny Mercer very well and she was attached to Capital Records, so if I would write some songs and send them out if they had any merit she'd show them to Johnny, which is what happened. I ran into Jack Segal and explained it to him and we sat down and started writing together. It was very easy to write together, and he and I were knocking things off one after another easily. It just seemed to come, and Johnny liked them, everybody liked them, so we were…
At the same time the material was shown to Louie Lipstone who was running the Paramount music department and Louie wanted us there, so suddenly we had a contract with Paramount
Pictures and with Capitol Records in one swelled swoop, if that's the terminology; that's how I got to the coast.
